conventions.convention: All spatial quantities use one named positively oriented inertial laboratory frame, x⁰=ct, SI units, c>0, μ₀>0 and ε₀=(μ₀c²)⁻¹. μ₀ is not assigned an exact measured numerical value.
Vacuum u=(ε₀|E|²+|B|²/μ₀)/2 and S=E×B/μ₀ are quadratic quantities. Locally integrable fields alone do not justify integrating their products; no distributional product is defined.
g=S/c², momentum flux Π=−σ, and tensor divergence is (div Π)ᵢ=Σⱼ∂ⱼΠᵢⱼ. Orbital angular quantities are x×g and (x×Π)ᵢₗ=ΣⱼₖεᵢⱼₖxⱼΠₖₗ, relative to the fixed chart origin.

General fixed-volume balances require Countable Choice, a specified finite piecewise C¹ boundary presentation, compact closure inside the spatial region, and outward normals. Boundary fluxes remain in the identities.

Matter energy and momentum balances are additional assumptions; symmetric matter momentum flux is required for the orbital angular balance. Each integrated total is constant throughout an interval exactly when its corresponding net boundary flux vanishes throughout that interval.
Vacuum plane waves use real k≠0, ω>0 and real-part encoding exp(i(k·x−ωt)). Zero amplitudes are allowed; nonzero Maxwell solutions require |k|=ω/c.

For e=a+id, the polarization trace is a cos θ−d sin θ. Zero amplitude belongs to the linear class. H=(a×d)·k̂; right-handed means H<0 and left-handed means H>0, with the stated incoming-wave screen orientation.

The whole-space Maxwell initial-value theorem assumes Countable Choice and constrained C∞ data; closed-slab regularity means extension to an open slab. Arbitrary growth is permitted. Finite-energy conservation is a conditional branch, with total energy defined by nonnegative ball exhaustion.

Period averages are deterministic averages at fixed position, not ensemble or detector averages. The plane-wave intensity is |⟨S⟩|=c⟨u⟩. Spatial fringe visibility at fixed phase differs from phase-scan visibility.
The isotropic Ohmic material branch is stated in its rest frame, with ε,μ>0 and σ≥0. κ=p+iq is the root of κ²=εμω²+iμσω with p>0 and q≥0. Skin depth is 1/q for σ>0 and +∞ for σ=0.

Complex dot and cross products are bilinear componentwise extensions; complex norms are Hermitian. On the noncompact plane, interface identities are explicit hypotheses, rather than applications of the compact-interface jump theorem.

Oblique Fresnel coefficients use electric amplitudes along fixed tangential directions. Incident admittances use the positive normal magnitude k₁₃; the reflected normal component is −k₁₃. Critical TM incidence is solved without defining ε₂ω/kₜ₃ at kₜ₃=0.

load_bearing.statement: For k∈R³\{0}, ω>0 and e,b∈C³, the encoded whole-space fields satisfy source-free smooth vacuum Maxwell if and only if k·e=k·b=0, k×e=ωb and k×b=−(ω/c²)e. Nonzero amplitude solutions exist if and only if |k|²=ω²/c². On dispersion, solutions are exactly (e,k×e/ω) with k·e=0; B=k̂×E/c and |B|=|E|/c pointwise.

Jointly C¹ fields satisfying smooth vacuum Maxwell with continuous sources obey ∂ₜu+div S=−J·E. Under Countable Choice and the specified fixed finite piecewise C¹ volume with compact closure inside Ω, d/dt∫u=−∫J·E−∮S·n. The matter-work interpretation additionally uses Lorentz coupling clause (ii); weak fields and singular-source products are excluded.

For explicit real-part plane waves with k∈C³, ω>0 in the declared scalar Ohmic medium, the four macroscopic equations with ρf=0 and Jf=σE hold if and only if k·e=k·h=0, k×e=ωμh and k×h=−(ωε+iσ)e. Nonzero solutions require k·k=εμω²+iμσω. The lossless real-k averages and the lossless evanescent factorization and zero normal averaged flux are established under their stated branch hypotheses.

For complex Y₁,Y₂ with Y₁+Y₂≠0, the system Ei+Er=Et and Y₁(Ei−Er)=Y₂Et gives r=(Y₁−Y₂)/(Y₁+Y₂), t=2Y₁/(Y₁+Y₂) when Ei≠0. If Ei=0, Er=Et=0 and field ratios are undefined. For real Y₁>0, the algebraic coefficients satisfy |r|²+(Re Y₂/Y₁)|t|²=1; purely imaginary Y₂ gives |r|=1 and t≠0.

Under smooth vacuum Maxwell, jointly C¹ fields, continuous sources and continuum Lorentz coupling, ∂ₜg−div σ=−f, equivalently ∂ₜg+div Π=−f, with f=ρE+J×B. The Countable-Choice fixed-volume branch gives d/dt∫gᵢ=∮Σⱼσᵢⱼnⱼ−∫fᵢ with its specified boundary presentation and compact containment.

Assuming Countable Choice, constrained C∞ whole-space data E₀,B₀ generate a jointly C∞ source-free Maxwell solution on [t₀,T], unique among jointly C² extension-sense solutions. Agreement of data and curls on the specified closed backward-cone base gives agreement at its vertex; compact support propagates within radius ρ+c(t−t₀). If initial ball-exhaustion energy is finite, it is conserved; ∫Bᵣ(x₀)u(x,t)≤∫Bᵣ₊c(t−s)(x₀)u(x,s) for r>0 and t₀≤s≤t≤T.

For every complex transverse vacuum plane-wave amplitude on dispersion, ⟨u⟩=ε₀|e|²/2, ⟨S⟩=c⟨u⟩k̂, ⟨g⟩=⟨S⟩/c² and ⟨σᵢⱼ⟩=−⟨u⟩k̂ᵢk̂ⱼ. These are exact period averages. Zero amplitude has zero energy; every nonzero whole-space amplitude has infinite box-exhaustion energy.

Pairwise distinct complex frequencies define linearly independent exponential characters on any nonempty open subset of Rⁿ, n≥1. A real-part-zero sum instead forces each grouped coefficient Σλⱼ=νcⱼ+Σλⱼ=−conj(ν)conj(cⱼ) to vanish; self-paired frequencies constrain only the real part.

concerns.concern: The Statement says the transmitted normal root 'is selected by non-growth in the x₃>0 half-space', then selects the positive real root in the propagating branch. Both positive and negative real roots have unit-modulus exponential factors and satisfy non-growth. The explicit positive-root convention makes the subsequent calculation well specified, but its stated justification should distinguish non-growth from the additional forward/outgoing propagating choice.
